profile.stagger_pattern: Annual April election (second Tuesday), 4-year terms, 6 council seats staggered two per ward: Ward I Seat A + Ward III Seat B in 2018/2022/2026; Mayor + Ward II Seat B in 2019/2023/2027; Ward I Seat B + Ward III Seat A in 2020/2024/2028; Ward II Seat A in 2021/2025/2029. The 2020 election was COVID-postponed from 2020-04-14 to 2020-06-16. No April 2026 election: the city moved to 2026-11-03 combined with the Minnehaha County general, extending the 2022 Ward I-A and Ward III-B terms.

gaps.attempted: City publishes council minutes only from Jan 2020 forward (cityofbrandon.org/agendas states 2020-current online, earlier by request). Constructed-URL sweep of the Catalis /uploads/MM-DD-YY.pdf minutes pattern for all 2019 Mondays returned 404 on every date; six alternative 2019 filename forms also 404. Wayback CDX over cityofbrandon.org (from=2019&to=2020) indexes only 256 captures, one PDF, and no archived Mayor & Council page. SD Legislative Audit index carries only Brandon City 2024.pdf; 2019-2023 and 2025 all 404. Ballotpedia's Brandon SD page is a stub with no officials. brandonvalleyjournal.com (Drupal 7) returns 404 on /search/node/ and /legals.
gaps.notes: The internal presiding officer for 2019 could not be established. Barb Fish is documented as Council President continuously from 2020-07-06 onward, but the earliest evidence is the 2020-07-06 organizational vote, which was a fresh nomination rather than a 'keep' motion, so it cannot be rolled back.

run_log.detail: South Dakota registry entry confirmed accurate on both counts. (a) State legislative audit reports ARE the structured source and the 'City Officials' page exists: legislativeaudit.sd.gov/reports/City/Brandon City 2024.pdf returned 200 with a Dec-31-2024 officials page (Mayor Harry Buck; board Fish, Marso, Kull, Lawrence, Steen, Johnson). (b) The registry's warning that 'the index shows only the most recent report per city' is exactly right: reports.aspx?type=City lists ONLY 'City/Brandon City 2024.pdf', and 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2025 all 404, as do 'Brandon 2019.pdf' and 'City of Brandon 2019.pdf'. No state or county results portal was attempted, per the registry.

BRIEFING ASSUMPTION CORRECTED: the task brief suggested 3-year terms producing an annual cycle. Brandon is aldermanic with SIX council members on FOUR-year terms, two per ward across three wards, plus a mayor elected at large to a four-year term (cityofbrandon.org/council). The annual cycle comes from the STAGGER, not from short terms: Ward I-A + Ward III-B in 2018/2022/2026; Mayor + Ward II-B in 2019/2023/2027; Ward I-B + Ward III-A in 2020/2024/2028; Ward II-A in 2021/2025/2029. Derived from cityofbrandon.org/uploads/dm/22311/Elected_Officials_Terms_20182031.pdf, a 2018-2031 term grid marking each seat's term starts (O), appointments (O*), predecessor terms (----) and future elections (X). Extraction note: pdftotext -layout spacing is unreliable on this grid; the columns were aligned by word bounding boxes via 'pdftotext -bbox-layout', which maps every mark onto a year centre to within 1.5pt. Independently corroborated by the city's 2026 NOTICE OF VACANCY, which lists exactly Ward 1 and Ward 3, four-year terms. Elections are the second Tuesday in April (confirmed in-document for 2020-04-14, 2021-04-13, 2022-04-12). CALENDAR CHANGE: there is no April 2026 city election; cityofbrandon.org/elections states the next city election is 2026-11-03, combined with the Minnehaha County general, with petitions circulating 2026-07-03 to 2026-08-18. The Ward I-A and Ward III-B terms are therefore running roughly seven months long.

South Dakota has no centralized municipal results, so the whole reconstruction ran off the city's own minutes at Rung 6. The Catalis CMS serves minutes as plain PDFs at a fully constructible URL: cityofbrandon.org/vertical/sites/%7B23CB10F0-8C35-4CA4-9AD1-B693F0F58E76%7D/uploads/MM-DD-YY.pdf. Sweeping every Monday 2019-01-01 to 2026-09-01 (400 candidate dates) yielded 135 regular-meeting minutes covering 2020-01-20 through 2026-08-03 at ZERO WebSearch cost. Each opens with a verbatim 'Present were ...' roll and an 'Absent:' line, giving a meeting-by-meeting membership series with no unobserved interval longer than about six weeks. Every cycle 2020-2025 was sourced from the 'CALL TO ORDER OF THE NEW COUNCIL' / Oath of Office item in the first May meeting, which names each new member WITH THEIR WARD. Two throttling notes for re-runs: parallel fetches above about 6 concurrent connections return nothing, and a plain 404 is served as a 906-byte stub rather than an error.

COVID: the 2020 cycle is not where it looks. The 2020-03-16 minutes appoint election workers for an 'April 14th Municipal Election'; the 2020-06-15 minutes then set a canvassing board for 'the election of June 16, 2020'. The election was postponed to 2020-06-16 and the new council seated 2020-07-06, which is why the 2020-05-04 minutes still show the OLD council including Chuck Parsons. Reading April 2020 as the seating date would have mis-dated three seats by three months and lost Parsons entirely.

SEVEN mid-term changes found, all dated from minutes. (1) 2021-03-01 Mayor Paul Lundberg's resignation accepted effective immediately. (2) The mayoralty then sat VACANT for roughly 15 weeks with Council President Barb Fish chairing; motions to appoint Alderman Jack Parliament failed on 2021-04-05, 2021-04-19 and again on 2021-05-03 (3-3, Clark/David/Parliament aye, Fish/Jorgenson/Kull nay). (3) Jim Heinitz was appointed mayor after applicant discussion on 2021-05-17 and first appears as Mayor on 2021-06-21. (4) 2022-03-07: no petition was filed for a Ward 3 seat, so it was 'deemed to be vacant' and had to be filled by appointment under state statute. (5) 2022-04-18: Colin Steen appointed to the Ward 3 vacancy effective 2022-05-02, with Alderwoman Vickie David recused — the recusal identifies it as HER seat. (6) 2022-07-18: 'Council Member Jack Parliament has submitted his resignation, effective immediately'; the other Ward III seat then sat vacant nine weeks until Bruce Johnson took the oath on 2022-09-19. (7) 2023-03-06: 'No petitions were filed for the one-year term in Ward 3, therefore a vacancy has been created' — Johnson's appointed term expired at the 2023 election and he was re-appointed rather than elected, which the terms grid records as a second O*. Note the structural tell the brief predicts: Ward 3 appears on the 2022, 2023 AND 2024 ballots, which is only explicable as unexpired terms.

2019 is the one weak year and it is an ABSENCE, not a block — cityofbrandon.org/robots.txt name-blocks only Googlebot/bingbot on /admin/ and /manager/, and served every file requested. Routes tried and failed: (a) the minutes URL pattern for all 24 Mondays of 2019 plus six alternative filename forms — 404 on every one; (b) SD Legislative Audit for 2019-2023 — 404, index holds 2024 only; (c) Wayback CDX (which does work, contra the project's dead-source list) — 'url=cityofbrandon.org&matchType=domain&from=2019&to=2020' returns 200 with only 256 captures, 207 of them HTML and exactly one PDF (Population_Estimates_2019.pdf); the uploads-path query returned 1,766 rows with no 2019 minutes; and 'web/2019*/cityofbrandon.org/council' resolves to a 2021-04-24 capture, so there is no archived 2019 roster page; (d) one WebSearch, which returned Brandon MANITOBA results plus the city's own current pages — the homonym trap is real and search is worthless here; (e) ballotpedia.org/Brandon,_South_Dakota fetched fine by curl (200, 124KB) but is a stub with federal and state officials only, no council; (f) brandonvalleyjournal.com is live Drupal 7 but /search/node/<terms> and /legals both 404. NOT tried, and the best remaining lead: the statutory publication of proceedings in the official newspaper's print/legal-notice archive, and the city's own offer of pre-2020 records on request.

Seat count holds at 7 (mayor + 6) in every observed roll call across 2020-2026, matching the aldermanic form. Ward assignments for all seven current holders come from cityofbrandon.org/council and are corroborated by the ward named in each oath-of-office entry. The 2024 audit report's officials page independently confirms the 2024 roster. Day-of-week check: 2019-04-09, 2020-06-16, 2021-04-13, 2022-04-12, 2023-04-11, 2024-04-09 and 2025-04-08 are all Tuesdays, and every seating date used is a Monday, matching the charter's first-and-third-Monday meeting rule. Names were read from locally extracted verbatim text (pdftotext -layout), never from a page summary. One near-miss worth recording: a naive surname match on 'David' matches 'David Kull' and silently kept Alderwoman Vickie David on the council two years after she left — the extraction masks 'David Kull' and 'Lisa Marso' (the city attorney, versus Alderman Randy Marso) before matching.

UNRESOLVED, flagged rather than hidden. (1) 2019 seat occupancy before the April 2019 election is unknown for five offices — Mayor, Ward I-B, Ward II-A, Ward II-B and Ward III-B — all of which the terms grid shows starting a term in 2019. The tenures recorded for those seats begin at the estimated 2019-05-06 seating, so the 2019 seat-year is covered but its first four months are attributed to nobody. Six of the seven 2019 holders are established only by rolling the January 2020 roll call backwards against the terms grid, hence the low/medium confidence. (2) The split of the two Ward III seats between Chuck Parsons and Vickie David in 2019-2020 is an inference: both Ward III seats were on the June 2020 ballot, David won the two-year unexpired term (she was recused from the 2022 appointment to her own seat, and Steen succeeded her) and Parliament won the four-year term, so Parsons is placed in the seat Parliament took. The ward is certain; the A/B seat label for 2019-2020 is not. (3) Jim Heinitz's appointment as mayor is dated to his first recorded appearance, 2021-06-21; the appointment vote itself falls between 2021-05-17 and 2021-06-21 and was not located. (4) Bruce Johnson's 2023 re-appointment is carried as a continuation of his 2022 appointed tenure rather than as a separate row, because no dated appointment record was found for it.

23 tenure rows, 8 cycles, 1 gap. Two seat-years are recorded as vacant in run_log rather than as gap rows, per the brief's rule against annotating an already-sourced seat-year: the mayoralty 2021-03-01 to 2021-06-21 and Ward III Seat A 2022-07-18 to 2022-09-19. Seat labels use 'Ward N Seat A/B' because the city numbers neither the two seats within a ward nor the wards' places; A/B are anchored to the two rows of the Elected Officials Terms grid and are stable across all years.
